company: Listed Investment Trust for which Equity Trustees Limited is the Responsible Entity (ACN 004 031 298, AFSL 240975), a wholly-owned subsidiary of EQT Holdings Limited
title: Listed Investment Trusts Trading Policy

tiers.name: EQT Persons
tiers.description: Directors, key management personnel, and all employees of EQTHL and/or any of its wholly or majority owned companies including the Responsible Entity, and contractors and consultants who may come into the possession of Inside Information.

tiers.name: Responsible Entity's directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Responsible Entity, a subset of EQT Persons, with an additional post-trade disclosure duty for ASX reporting purposes.

tiers.name: LIT Partners
tiers.description: Persons or entities engaged or contracted with the Responsible Entity in managing and/or administering a LIT (e.g. the investment manager). Trade under their own trading policy, procedures and/or controls agreed with the Responsible Entity, subject to minimum standards, and must disclose LIT Person transactions to the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: LIT Persons
tiers.description: Directors, employees, contractors and consultants of a LIT Partner, or any other related account as defined by the LIT Partner's trading policy.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A spouse, partner or child of an EQT Person, or any other person whom the EQT Person may be expected to control or have significant influence over, including other immediate family members, business partners, companies or other entities or trusts. Must seek clearance through their EQT Person, LIT Person or LIT Partner.

definitions.hedging_definition: hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding LIT Units

windows.end_anchor: one (1) hour after the Responsible Entity releases the next estimated Net Tangible Asset per Unit (NTA) or Net Asset Value (NAV) of the Fund
one (1) hour after the Responsible Entity releases the next estimated NTA or NAV of the Fund

windows.start_anchor: the earlier of 28 calendar days before (if known), or the day the decision is made to proceed with, a PDS, prospectus or similar disclosure document
windows.end_anchor: the next full business day after the PDS, prospectus or similar disclosure document is lodged by the Responsible Entity with the ASX

windows.start_anchor: 28 calendar days before a general meeting of unitholders
windows.end_anchor: the next full business day after the general meeting

windows.start_anchor: the date the Responsible Entity makes the decision to buy-back units in a LIT (applies only to EQT Persons who have knowledge of the buy-back and are involved in its day to day management)
windows.end_anchor: the next full business day after the buy-back has been completed

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Responsible Entity may specify 'any other period' as an additional Black-out Period (clause defining Black-out Period, item (v)); the policy does not state whether such a designation is confidential. Where the FY/HY and PDS/prospectus Black-out Periods overlap, the PDS/prospectus period governs.

rules.detail: 'Trade' is defined broadly as buying, selling or transferring 'any economic interest' in Units. An OTC put/call over Units transfers economic interest and so falls within this definition, requiring the same written prior clearance, absence of Inside Information, and avoidance of Black-out Periods as any other Trade.
rules.evidence: Trade or Trading means to buy, sell or transfer any economic interest in Units, including electing to vary a dividend reinvestment plan ("DRP") participation.

rules.detail: Hedging or other financial arrangements limiting the economic risk of holding LIT Units are expressly permitted only with prior clearance under the Trading Request Procedure; there is no outright prohibition and no vesting concept (this is a trust, not an employee incentive scheme).
rules.evidence: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding LIT Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or similar structure operates to limit the economic risk of holding Units and so falls within the same clearance-gated hedging/financial-arrangement restriction as express hedging.
rules.evidence: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding LIT Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy; only short-term/speculative trading (Section 6(i)) and hedging (Section 6(ii)) are addressed as restricted trading categories.

CFDs are not named but transfer 'economic interest' in Units (bringing them within the Trade definition) and, if used to limit exposure, also fall within the hedging/financial-arrangement restriction in 6(ii); either way, prior clearance under the Trading Request Procedure is required.
rules.evidence: Trade or Trading means to buy, sell or transfer any economic interest in Units

rules.detail: Margin lending is not banned outright: it is expressly permitted with prior clearance approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.
rules.evidence: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: Granting any form of security over Units is expressly permitted with prior clearance under the Trading Request Procedure; this is a standalone Restricted Trading rule, not part of the 'Trade' definition itself.
rules.evidence: may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: The prohibition extends to 'any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units', not just margin loans, so any secured financing is captured; all are permitted only with prior clearance under the Trading Request Procedure.
rules.evidence: may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: Trading in or out of Units on market within three months of acquisition is permitted only with prior clearance under the Trading Request Procedure.
rules.evidence: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not engage in short-term or speculative trading in a LIT's Units, i.e. trading in or out of the Units on market within three (3) months of acquiring them, unless written prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary of the Responsible Entity
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary of the Responsible Entity (evidence of executed trade)
clearance.evidence: A written request for clearance to trade is to be submitted to, and approval received from, the Responsible Entity's Company Secretary. A clearance to trade can be given, withdrawn, or refused without a reason being given. The decision is final and binding. Any clearance refusal or withdrawal must be kept confidential by the person who sought clearance, and may not be disclosed to anyone. A clearance to trade is valid for five (5) business days.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary of the Responsible Entity
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary of the Responsible Entity
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of any trade
clearance.evidence: Within two (2) business days of any trade, the Responsible Entity's directors must provide written confirmation to the Company Secretary of the nature, price and quantity of Units traded, to ensure that the requisite information is lodged with the ASX within the prescribed reporting time.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary of the Responsible Entity (register of transactions, kept confidential)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 7 days of execution of the transaction, or as otherwise agreed in writing
clearance.evidence: LIT Partners must disclose to the Company Secretary of the Responsible Entity any transaction undertaken in a LIT Unit by a LIT Person within 7 days of execution of the transaction, or as otherwise agreed in writing with the Responsible Entity (LIT Partner Transactions).

carve_outs: written prior clearance approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure
short_term.evidence: may not engage in short-term or speculative trading in a LIT's Units, i.e. trading in or out of the Units on market within three (3) months of acquiring them, unless written prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

exceptions.evidence: Those that do not result in a change to the beneficial interest in the Units (such as transferring Units already held personally into a superannuation fund), and where prior written notification has been given to the Company Secretary
an acquisition of Units under the LIT's distribution reinvestment plan, excluding an election to vary participation.

exceptions.approver: Responsible Entity's Chair (or the EQTHL Board Risk Committee Chair in the case of proposed trading by the Responsible Entity's Chair)
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship, where EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners have pressing financial commitments that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling Units

exceptions.approver: Responsible Entity's Chair (or the EQTHL Board Risk Committee Chair in the case of proposed trading by the Responsible Entity's Chair)
exceptions.evidence: requirements under a court order or court enforceable undertakings or other legal or regulatory requirements

exceptions.approver: Responsible Entity's Chair (or the EQTHL Board Risk Committee Chair in the case of proposed trading by the Responsible Entity's Chair)
exceptions.evidence: any other exceptional circumstances as determined by the Responsible Entity's Chair (or the EQTHL Board Risk Committee Chair in the case of proposed trading by the Responsible Entity's Chair)

financing_disclosure: EQT Persons/LIT Persons/LIT Partners, at inception, must obtain prior written clearance under the Trading Request Procedure before entering a margin loan or granting any form of security over Units (Section 6(iii))

external_documents: LIT Partner's own trading policy, procedures and/or controls (as agreed with the Responsible Entity)
exemption_authority: The Responsible Entity's Chair (or the EQTHL Board Risk Committee Chair, if the Chair is the one proposing to trade) determines whether 'exceptional circumstances' exist (severe financial hardship, court order/enforceable undertaking or other legal/regulatory requirement, or other circumstances), with the Company Secretary consulting the Chair on any such proposed trading; however, irrespective of any clearance or exceptional circumstances, a person in possession of Inside Information is always prohibited from trading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into hedging ... margin lending ... or short-term or speculative trading ... unless ... clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: All three collar-relevant activities – the derivative hedge, the security grant for the loan, and any early unwind – are expressly permitted subject only to prior clearance, none is an outright ban, making this one of the more funded-collar-friendly policies reviewed, provided clearance is obtained and the blackout/insider-trading conditions are separately satisfied.

bespoke_clauses.topic: refusal confidentiality duty on the applicant
bespoke_clauses.clause: Any clearance refusal or withdrawal must be kept confidential by the person who sought clearance, and may not be disclosed to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually, it is the executive (not the Responsible Entity) who must keep a refusal or withdrawal confidential, so the executive could not explain to the bank counterparty why a scheduled collar leg did not proceed without itself breaching the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: EQT Persons may trade in a LIT's Units provided they are not in the possession of Inside Information, the trade does not take place during a Black-out Period, and written prior clearance to trade has been approved.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance alone cannot authorise trading during a Black-out Period; only the Chair-level 'exceptional circumstances' process (Section 8) can potentially permit that, so collar entry, unwind, roll or settlement should be timed for open windows or a bespoke Chair-level exception sought.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (No exclusion for a lender-exercised or forced disposal appears in Section 7's list of excluded trades.)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike some peer policies, there is no express exemption if the bank needs to enforce its security and sell the collateral Units during a Black-out Period; absent a bespoke waiver, that sale would need Section 8 exceptional-circumstances clearance from the Chair.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Trade or Trading means to buy, sell or transfer any economic interest in Units, including electing to vary a dividend reinvestment plan ("DRP") participation.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The substance-based 'any economic interest' test means an OTC derivative referencing the Units, and not just an on-market sale, is treated as a Trade subject to the general blackout/clearance regime in addition to the specific Section 6 hedging clearance.

summary: A funded collar is workable in principle under this policy, subject to conditions, because none of its three relevant restrictions is an outright ban: Section 6 expressly permits EQT Persons (and LIT Persons/LIT Partners) to enter hedging or other risk-limiting financial arrangements, to grant security over Units (including margin lending), and to trade within three months of acquisition, in each case with prior written clearance under the Trading Request Procedure from the Responsible Entity's Company Secretary. That clearance is valid for five business days, can be given, withdrawn or refused without reasons (with the refusal itself being an outcome the applicant, not the Responsible Entity, must keep confidential), and does not amount to an endorsement of the trade. Critically, clearance can never authorise dealing during a Black-out Period (tied to NTA/NAV releases, PDS/prospectus lodgements, general meetings, or buy-backs) or while in possession of Inside Information, and no lender-forced-sale exemption is provided, so execution, roll and unwind of the collar's legs should be scheduled outside those windows or run through the Chair-level exceptional-circumstances process. Because this is a trust with no employee equity incentive scheme, there is no unvested/vested-locked distinction to navigate. Overall verdict: workable with clearance, subject to the blackout calendar and the absence of any forced-sale carve-out for the bank's security.
